entries.title: Slack: ask Sessionboard about your events and get notifications in Slack
entries.summary: The **Slack** app is in **Apps** for every organization. Connect your workspace once, and each person can turn on the **Slack** column in their notification preferences to get Sessionboard notifications as Slack messages. Organizations hosted in the United States with AI features on can also ask about their event data in the app's chat, with `/sessionboard`, or by @mentioning it in a channel — answers run under each person's own Sessionboard permissions.

enable.path: Apps → Slack → Set up Slack → Connect with Slack

where.path: Apps → Slack; in Slack: the Sessionboard app, /sessionboard, @Sessionboard; notification preferences → Slack column

entries.use_case: Your team gets answers about speakers, sessions and submissions where they already work, without opening Sessionboard, and notifications land in Slack with a link back to the record.

cs_action.note: Self-serve from Apps. Needs AI features on for the org; askers need a Sessionboard account with the same email as their Slack account.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any team that lives in Slack and asks 'how many speakers have confirmed?' type questions, or wants notifications outside email.
internal.who_should_get_it: US-hosted organizations with AI features on. EU and Middle East organizations can connect and receive Slack notifications, but questions asked in Slack are answered for US-hosted organizations only.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Slack (staff see the same page). Usage and installs post to #engineering-logs-team-lead once the activity log ships.
internal.gotchas: @mention answers are visible to the whole channel; /sessionboard and the app's chat are private. /sessionboard doesn't work inside threads. Slack guests and people from other organizations in shared channels are refused. One Slack workspace per Sessionboard organization.
internal.talk_track: Connect Slack once and your whole team can ask Sessionboard questions right in Slack — each person only sees what they can see in Sessionboard.
